subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is a constant in a program?
options: A value that cannot change while the program runs
A value that changes every time the program runs
A memory location that stores user input
A subroutine that returns a fixed result
questions.explain: A constant is given a value once and that value stays fixed for the whole execution of the program.

questions.q: What does the MOD operator return?
options: The whole-number result of a division
The result raised to a power
questions.explain: MOD (modulus) gives the remainder left over when one integer is divided by another.

questions.q: What does the DIV operator do?
options: Performs integer (whole-number) division, discarding the remainder
Returns the remainder of a division
Divides and gives a decimal result
Rounds a real number to the nearest integer
questions.explain: DIV carries out integer division, giving only the whole-number quotient and ignoring any remainder.

questions.q: Which of these is a data type used in the OCR specification?
questions.explain: The OCR specification uses the data types integer, real, Boolean, character and string.

questions.q: In the OCR reference language, what is the index of the first element of an array?
questions.explain: Arrays are zero-indexed, so the first element is at position 0.

questions.q: In the OCR reference language, which function opens an existing file so its contents can be read?
questions.explain: openRead() opens a file for reading, and readLine() is then used to read a line from it.

questions.q: What are the three basic programming constructs?
questions.explain: All algorithms can be built from sequence, selection and iteration.

questions.q: Why might a programmer use a named constant such as VAT = 0.20 instead of typing 0.20 throughout the code?
options: It makes the code easier to read and change the value in one place
It makes the program run more slowly on purpose
It prevents the program from using any variables
It automatically converts the number to a string
questions.explain: A named constant improves readability and means the value only has to be changed once if it needs updating.

questions.q: How does a do...until loop differ from a while loop?
options: A do...until loop always runs its body at least once because the condition is tested at the end
A do...until loop can never run its body
A do...until loop tests its condition before running the body
A do...until loop must always be count-controlled
questions.explain: Because the condition is checked after the body, a do...until loop executes at least once, unlike a while loop which checks first.

questions.q: A for loop is best described as which type of iteration?
questions.explain: A for loop repeats a set number of times, so it is count-controlled iteration.

questions.q: What is the purpose of casting with int("7")?
options: It converts the string "7" into the integer 7
It converts the integer 7 into the string "7"
It rounds 7 down to the nearest ten
It checks whether "7" is a valid number
questions.explain: Casting with int() changes a value's data type into an integer so it can be used in calculations.

questions.q: The Boolean expression (A AND B) is true only when...
options: Both A and B are true
At least one of A or B is true
Both A and B are false
A is true and B is false
questions.explain: The AND operator gives true only if every condition it joins is true.

questions.q: What does the operation name.length return when name holds the string "Delta"?
questions.explain: The length operation counts the characters in the string, and "Delta" contains five characters.

questions.q: What does the declaration array board[8,8] create?
options: A two-dimensional array with 8 rows and 8 columns
Two separate arrays each of 8 elements
questions.explain: Two indices in the declaration create a 2D array, here an 8 by 8 grid of elements.

questions.q: What is the value of 17 MOD 5?
questions.explain: 17 divided by 5 is 3 remainder 2, so 17 MOD 5 is 2.

questions.q: In the OCR reference language, what does "computer".substring(2,3) return?
questions.explain: substring(2,3) starts at zero-based index 2 ('m') and returns 3 characters, giving "mpu".

questions.q:
Given x = 8, what is printed?
if x > 10 then
  print("A")
elseif x > 5 then
  print("B")
else
  print("C")
endif
questions.explain: x is not greater than 10 but is greater than 5, so the elseif branch runs and "B" is printed.

questions.q:
How many times does the body of this loop execute?
for i = 1 to 5
  print(i)
next i
questions.explain: The loop counts from 1 to 5 inclusive, so the body runs five times.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Computer Science (J277) specification; Programming Fundamentals
